subject: FalconPay throughput surge & tail-latency — exec ops heartbeat
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@falconpay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: sudden throughput drop & 5% error spike — immediate help needed

Vivek —

We started seeing a major regression at 08:05 UTC: throughput collapsed (~60% drop) and error rate spiked to ~5% (baseline ~0.2%). 95p tail latency for our checkout route jumped from ~180ms to 1.2s. This is affecting checkout throughput and customers are seeing retries. We've collected a short telemetry snapshot and an error trace (attached).

Our engineers have verified this is happening across regions (primary US cluster) and it looks correlated with a backend model rollout from your side (we saw product_version: rwd-2028-07-20-0818 in the headers). We need a coordinated war-room and an exec-level status—this is impacting our SLAs.

Please advise immediate mitigation and ETA on fix/fallback.

—Samira
Samira Khan | Head of Platform Ops, FalconPay
ops@falconpay.com
Attachment: error-traces-20280720.log (13MB)

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop & 5% error spike — immediate help needed

Samira —

Thank you for the heads up and for attaching the traces. I’m escalating this to an exec ops channel now and we’ll stand up a war-room.

Immediate actions I’m putting in motion:
- War-room link (see internal mail) — join now for live triage.
- Rolling rollback to previous model variant (rwd-2028-07-18-stable) as a safety fallback — kick-off in 5m if we confirm rollback safe.
- Short-term throttling policy to protect the checkout path while we stabilize.

We’ll provide an external status update in ~30 minutes. I’m looping in Marissa (on-call telemetry), Laura (customer liaison), and Aditya (serving/runtime).

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Team —

FalconPay is seeing a large throughput regression + error spike tied to a model rollout. Please join the war-room (calendar invite sent) if you can: immediate triage. Quick asks:

- Aditya: confirm whether the new variant touches any kernel or compilation changes that could trigger regressions (quantization/kvcache changes).

Vivek

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: War-room now: FalconPay throughput/error escalation (link in calendar)

On 2028-07-20 08:25 UTC Vivek wrote:
> Team — FalconPay is seeing a large throughput regression + error spike tied to a model rollout. Please join the war-room...

Quick diagnostics:
- Telemetry (08:00–08:12): 95p p50/p95/p99 = 120ms / 310ms / 1.1s (spike window 08:04–08:09).
- Error breakdown: ~78% are inference-timeouts (model execution exceeding 800ms), ~12% are client timeouts due to retry backpressure, rest are protobuf decode errors.
- GPU metrics: host-side queues spiked, NVLink transfer times + kernel queue depth higher than normal for the new build.
- Autoscaler: scaled up 3 nodes at 08:06 but by then queue had built and prefix/KV cache cold-starts amplified latency.

Immediate recommendation: roll back to rwd-2028-07-18-stable (no kernel changes) and suspend automated rollout pipeline until post-mortem. I’ve uploaded a concise snapshot to the shared drive.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: falconpay-telemetry-snaps.zip

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: War-room now: FalconPay throughput/error escalation (link in calendar)

Marissa — thanks for the quick analysis. A few technical notes from the serving/runtime side:
- The build rwd-2028-07-20-0818 included a new attention kernel fallback for long sequences and a micro-optimization for KV cache compaction. Those touched the execution planner and kernel selection logic. We suspected low risk but will revert.
- Rolling back to rwd-2028-07-18-stable should be non-disruptive; I’m staging the rollback now and will push a safe canary to 10% first for validation.
- If rollback isn’t sufficient, we have an emergency routing policy to pin FalconPay to dedicated pool (if they accept traffic cutover) — that requires confirmation from commercial/legal for a short-term override.

I’ll post each deployment step to the runbook link.

—Aditya
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@falconpay.com>

Subject: FalconPay status update — mitigation plan underway

Samira —

Quick status from the war-room: we identified the likely cause as a recent runtime/kernel change in the 2028-07-20 build. Actions in motion:
1) Rolling back to rwd-2028-07-18-stable (canary 10% now; full rollback if validation passes).
2) Temporary throttling on non-checkout routes to protect checkout QPS.
3) Telemetry snapshot and error traces uploaded to the shared drive (link below).
4) We will provide a follow-up in 30 minutes with rollback validation metrics (p95/p99, error-rate, and throughput).

We know this is high-impact — Laura will follow up with FalconPay leadership with the same summary.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
